Startup with Canadian and UK team, incorporated to commercialise a new vehicle class, incorporating iOT/satellite networking to a ‘stability map’ (machine/reinforcement-learned stability location:conditions LLM) to enable safe integration of powered-vehicles into pedestrianised areas, and public-transit.
We’re a diverse team of seven individuals who love to build solutions to problems that affect the quality of people’s lives.
Our vision is to greatly reduce road-traffic related deaths and serious injury of pedestrians, while simultaneously deleting the stigma of using seated (Accessible) personal-mobility.
Our ambition is to move road-safety focus, from high-cost activities; 1000s of Km of segregated cycle-lanes, and upgraded road-vehicle eNCAP standards, - to enabling vulnerable journey-makers to ride on pavements where it’s safer to do so.
We believe there is a $25Bn underserved and currently disenfranchised, market opportunity for this new vehicle-class, alongside its positive social and environmental benefits.

Company description: The Common Wadden Sea Secretariat (CWSS) supports, facilitates and coordinates the Trilateral Wadden Sea Cooperation (TWSC). Located in Wilhelmshaven, the Secretariat was founded in 1987 by the Wadden Sea states Denmark, Germany, and the Netherlands.
The Secretariat
- coordinates, promotes and supports activities of the Cooperation;
- is responsible for the preparation and production of documents for ministerial conferences, meetings of the Wadden Sea Board (WSB) and trilateral work groups;
- collects and evaluates information on monitoring, protection and the ecological condition of the entire Wadden Sea;
- is the central contact for the UNESCO Wadden Sea World Heritage;
- produces and publishes reports by the Cooperation;
- involves the public in the protection of the entire Wadden Sea area through communications, awareness building and environmental education.
Since the inscription of the Wadden Sea on the UNESCO World Heritage List, the Secretariat moreover deals with the implementation of the obligations derived from the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.
The legal status and the functions of and regulations governing CWSS are stipulated in the Administrative Agreement concluded between the Danish, Dutch and German Ministries responsible for the Wadden Sea. Each Ministry finances a third of its budget. The working language of the Trilateral Cooperation and the CWSS is English.

INGECID S.L. is an engineering firm founded in 2009, with its headquarters in Santander and offices in Madrid and Bilbao, as well as international subsidiaries in Germany, Norway, South Africa, and the United States. Its corporate purpose is to conduct research and innovation in the fields of construction technology, software engineering, renewable energy, and nuclear energy, collaborating with research groups on the development of R&D projects. Innovation is a central element of its business strategy, which has resulted throughout its history in the generation of a large number of national and international patents and in the delivery of high-value-added technological solutions to the market.
INGECID has a multidisciplinary technical team of approximately 100 people (40% women), organized into areas of activity that include the management and development of R&D&I projects, software development, generative design, structural engineering, technical consulting, and radiological engineering, among others. As a certified entity, it has an R&D&I management unit composed of a specialized research team.
The company has established an Integrated Management System certified to the ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, UNE-EN ISO/IEC 27001:2022, and UNE-EN ISO 56001:2024, whose scope encompasses training, research, development, and innovation in projects and software in the fields of civil engineering, renewable energy, and nuclear energy. The company’s own resources allocated to R&D include design, programming, and data analysis tools; BIM software; and the VIRCORE platform (developed by INGECID) which is used as a collaborative project management environment.

entityName: University of Passau - Chair of Computer Networks and Computer Communications
entityDescription:
The Chair of Computer Networks And Computer Communications at the University of Passau has its main areas of research in satellite communication, network analysis and virtualization, self-organizing systems, IT security, safety and energy efficiency.
In regard to satellites, the team's research assesses the potential of satellite technologies for the energy system, particularly of satellite communications and Earth observation. In Earth observation, the team's interest is in studying how satellites can enhance situational awareness by acting as an additional source of information and by processing data at the edge. In satellite communications, the research focuses on how satellites can contribute to the resilience of the power grid, for example by providing a redundant communication path.
The Chair of Computer Networks And Computer Communications has experience in satellite communications from both completed and ongoing projects: In EnerSat, a feasibility study, satellite networks were studied for reliable monitoring of critical infrastructure. In STARS, the potential of satellite communication to combat blackouts was assessed. In KRISNet a flat sat is being developed to demonstrate multi-channel communication via both terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to enhance the resilience of the power grid.

description:
First Light Fusion operates a globally unique capability for reproducing, measuring and modelling extreme physical environments relevant to space systems. Originating from inertial fusion research, we bring together hypervelocity impact testing, extreme pressure and radiation environments, world-class diagnostics, and AI-driven data science and simulation. This integrated capability delivers assurance-grade experimental data and validated predictive insight in regimes that are difficult, or impossible, to access using conventional space test infrastructure. These capabilities directly support spacecraft resilience, shielding design, subsystem survivability, radiation effects assessment, and digital engineering for space missions. Capabilities Integrated testing, diagnostics and simulation for space-grade assurance. 
Hypervelocity Impact Testing — Up to 14 km/s 
We operate the UK's largest two-stage light gas gun and one of the most capable systems worldwide. Patented velocity amplifier technology accelerates projectiles from 0.1 km/s to greater than 14 km/s for controlled, repeatable, highly instrumented hypervelocity impact experiments. Access to the 10–14 km/s regime is globally unique and extends beyond conventional testing facilities, delivering critical experimental data for spacecraft qualification and mission assurance. 
Extreme Pressure, Shock & Radiation Environments 
A suite of patented amplifier technologies, manufactured in-house, provides access to extreme pressure, shock, thermal and radiation environments at significantly lower cost and faster iteration than large national facilities. First Light Fusion also operates the second-largest pulsed power facility in the world (and the largest in the UK), generating multi-megaampere currents, multi-megabar magnetic pressures, extreme pulsed X-ray and K-shell radiation environments, and transient plasma and electromagnetic loading. 
Diagnostics, Data Quality & Experimental Validation 
All experimental platforms are supported by world-class diagnostics, enabling high-resolution, time-resolved measurement of extreme events: ultra-high-speed optical imaging, velocity interferometry and shock diagnostics, time-resolved optical and X-ray measurements, and post-test material and structural characterisation. The emphasis is on generating assurance-grade datasets suitable for space qualification, model validation and digital engineering workflows, with full traceability and reproducibility aligned to ESA and ECSS testing expectations. Intelligence & Engineering Excellence From experiment to digital twin. 
AI, Data Science & Simulation 
A defining strength is the tight integration of physical experimentation with advanced data science and AI-driven simulation: high-fidelity hydrodynamic, structural and MHD modelling; physics-informed machine learning; reduced-order and surrogate modelling; uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis; and sovereign high-performance computing. Experimental data is used to validate, calibrate and extend predictive models, enabling reliable extrapolation beyond directly testable regimes and supporting digital twins and mission-level decision-making. 
A Powerful Capability for Space 
Experimental and computational infrastructure located in the UK providing access to national laboratory style facilities to support sensitive space programmes and early-stage validation. First Light enables faster iteration, lower programme risk, and world leading capability.

Forestio.ai, operated by Generation Forest s.r.o. in Prague, is an environmental technology startup focused on global reforestation and rainforest protection. Its mission is to empower individuals and businesses to combat climate change through transparent, tech-driven forest conservation.
The platform allows users to support either reforestation projects (planting new trees) or protection projects (safeguarding existing rainforests). Once selected, each forest is digitized and tracked using satellite imagery and analytical tools that monitor carbon sequestration, vegetation health, and environmental risks. Users receive quarterly reports with data and imagery showing the impact of their contribution.
A distinctive feature of Forestio.ai is its use of blockchain technology. Each digital forest is represented as an NFT, ensuring unique ownership and transparency, while CO₂ credits are issued as fungible tokens on the Polygon blockchain, with one token representing 1 kg of sequestered carbon. This system provides both traceability and credibility in climate impact reporting.

entityDescription:
Meccanica 42 S.r.l. is an Italian engineering company specialized in the development of advanced mechatronic systems, special-purpose vehicles, and testing and validation solutions for high-performance and safety-critical applications. The company combines mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering capabilities to design, integrate, and deploy innovative products from concept definition to operational validation.
Originally established in the automotive sector, Meccanica 42 supports vehicle manufacturers, technology suppliers, motorsport organizations, and research institutions in the development of complex vehicle functions and advanced mobility technologies. The company delivers real-time test systems, embedded control devices, and customized vehicle platforms, including demonstrators and special-purpose vehicles designed for research, validation, and operational activities. 
A distinctive strength of Meccanica 42 is its ability to bridge simulation, laboratory testing, and real-world deployment. Through the integration of hardware, software, sensors, actuators, and control systems, the company develops solutions that operate reliably in demanding environments where precision, safety, and performance are critical.
In addition to proprietary products, Meccanica 42 provides system integration, engineering consultancy, commissioning, technical support, and the development of customer-specific equipment and vehicles. This end-to-end approach enables customers to accelerate innovation, reduce development risks, and transform complex technical requirements into deployable solutions. 
Based in Sesto Fiorentino, Italy, Meccanica 42 operates dedicated engineering offices, laboratories, and workshops and invests continuously in research and development to expand its technologies beyond automotive applications into other sectors requiring advanced mechatronics, automation, and reliability-focused engineering.

Meccanica 42 is particularly interested in applying its expertise in mechatronic systems, special-purpose vehicles, embedded electronics, remote operations, and complex system integration to environmental monitoring, emergency response, and space-enabled services.

lean hardware

RISC-V is a family of open instruction sets for microprocessors. The V extension is for vector operations, underpinning signal processing, machine learning and AI. There are open designs of implementation for the V extension that run at about one watt.

lean software

micrograd (https://github.com/brief-ds/micrograd) is a 500-line machine learning library. It is easy to learn and innovate with, yet competitive in performance. It paves the way for simplifying attention-based models.

generic causal prediction

Our company specializes in advanced Research and Development across the fields of satellite communications, mobile networks, artificial intelligence, and next-generation digital technologies.
We have extensive expertise in the design, development, and validation of satellite-based communication systems, with a particular focus on Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, integrated terrestrial–non-terrestrial networks, and innovative communication architectures for future connectivity services.
In the telecommunications sector, we are actively involved in the study, simulation, optimization, and deployment of 5G and emerging 6G network technologies. entityName: UNIVERSITAET KLAGENFURT - Control of Networked Systems Group
entityDescription:
The Control of Networked Systems Group (CNS) is part of the Institute of Smart Systems Technologies at the University of Klagenfurt (Austria) and the engaged research activities cover control theory, state estimation and motion planning, modeling of dynamic systems, simulation, and (mobile) robot automation in multi-agent scenarios. We pursue these activities both from a classical and data-driven AI perspective. The field of interests include, but are not limited to, the following: Collaborative (mobile) robot autonomy in 3D space, state estimation aware control and motion planning, on-board environment perception and decision making, long-term task execution in changing environments, networked mission planning for multiple agents. The Control of Networked Systems Group seeks to push the current limits in AI supported state estimation, cooperative visual perception, and multi-modal sensor fusion for autonomous and networked systems. 

Key Research Facilities, Infrastructure, and Equipment:
There is direct access to a 150m² drone hall to test drone and other (mobile) robotic related frameworks. The hall features a volume of more than 1,300m³ with a high-precision tracking system, a cable robot to emulate low-gravity environments, and high-performance computer units for AI training. 
Additionally, an outdoor arena with 1,000m2 and 15,000m3 volume will be available with an identical tracking system.

Our Expertise
* GNSS independent modular sensor fusion: Resilient equivariant methods (vision, radar, IR, lidar, UWB, etc)
* Data alignment across different reference frames using real-time sensor fusion and state estimation
* Self-aware and self-calibrating robotic systems able to re-calibrate and re-initialize online with self-healing capabilities
* Heterogeneous multi-agent collaborative state estimation and sensor fusion onboard compute constraint platforms
* Application oriented implementation on real platforms, large RAS test and validation facilities (1’300m³ indoor, 15’000m³ outdoor)

entityDescription: Hyperplan is an enterprise crop intelligence platform that turns parcel-level, in-season field data into commercial and supply decisions—not agronomic prescriptions—for agribusiness teams. It serves three buyer segments: input manufacturers and distributors, commodity traders, and cooperatives, each using field-level foresight to decide where and when to act before the season (and market) shifts. The platform runs across 35+ countries and 250M+ hectares monitored, with 59 organizations on board, including 9 of the top 15 global input manufacturers. Its technical foundation is a layered data stack—field boundary detection, crop classification, which in turn powers in-season monitoring and market insights.

entityDescription:
Embever is a Magdeburg-based German technology company founded in 2017 that develops secure, low-power Internet of Things (IoT) solutions for industrial companies and original equipment manufacturers. Its goal is to help manufacturers transform conventional equipment into connected, intelligent products without having to build the complete hardware, connectivity, firmware, cloud, and integration infrastructure themselves.
Embever provides engineering services covering hardware design, antenna development, firmware and protocol implementation, certification, dashboards, and integration with enterprise systems. Its focus is particularly on reliable, battery-powered and industrial-grade devices, including retrofit solutions for existing equipment.

entityDescription:
At Fraunhofer IWES, we are continuously working on optimizing wind energy and hydrogen technologies. With its research services, IWES makes a significant contribution to advancing the energy transition and substantially decreasing the associated costs. Our expertise and unique test infrastructure allow us to systematically identify and minimize development risks in new products and systems. In this way, we help to accelerate the certification and time to market of innovative products while simultaneously increasing their quality level. By doing so, we contribute to their reliable functionality and transparent financing.
IWES boosts innovation strength with its participation in many development projects in the wind industry and a wide variety of registered patents. We are making significant contributions to the energy transition for a global future worth living. Find out more about our vision, how important sustainability is to us, and what the symbiotic relationship between wind energy and hydrogen means for the energy system of the near future.

entityDescription:
GDL Innovation SA is a Swiss deep-tech company pioneering explicit, non-anthropomorphic spatial AI. Its core technology, the SGDL Exolanguage, is the first Multidimensional Logical World Model Language: a symbolic reasoning system grounded in primitive recursive functions, n-dimensional projective geometry and exact integer (bignum) arithmetic, originating from research at the Université de Montréal in the 1990s.
Unlike statistical AI, which extracts implicit intelligence from data, the Exolanguage encodes spatial intelligence explicitly — making geometry, topology, indexing and encoding exact, reversible and fully auditable. The system serves as the logical counterpart to learned world models, with applications ranging from digital twins and neuro-symbolic AI (explicit spatial priors for foundation models) to HPC-scale rendering and indexation, currently deployed on the Alps supercomputer at CSCS (Lugano). The company's technology is protected by international patents.

entityDescription:
InGeoLab S.r.l. is an Italian multidisciplinary engineering company established in 2016, providing advanced technical services in civil and environmental engineering, Earth sciences, structural diagnostics, infrastructure monitoring and risk assessment.
The company combines engineering expertise with innovative technologies, including Earth Observation, InSAR, remote sensing, GIS, geophysics, numerical modelling and advanced monitoring systems, developing integrated solutions for infrastructure and environmental applications.
Research & Development is a key component of InGeoLab's strategy. The company actively develops and tests innovative methodologies by integrating satellite observations, ground-based monitoring, advanced data processing and digital technologies. InGeoLab's commitment to innovation has also been recognised within the SMAU Innovation Award framework.
InGeoLab operates according to a structured quality and sustainability-oriented management approach. The company is certified according to UNI EN ISO 9001:2015 and UNI/PdR 125:2022, and is currently undergoing the certification process for ISO/IEC 27001, strengthening its information security and data management framework.
Through the combination of engineering expertise, applied R&D and digital innovation, InGeoLab aims to transform advanced monitoring technologies and Earth Observation data into operational decision-support solutions for infrastructure managers, public authorities and industrial stakeholders.
